messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bengali, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bengali line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
তিনি ভূমি বা পণ্য খাবেন না, কিন্তু জ্ঞান, প্রেম এবং বীরত্ব, এবং তার জন্মস্থান ফেল্ত্রো এবং ফেল্ত্রোর মধ্যে হবে।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Questi | demonstrative pronoun “this one” (the subject) | তিনি | “he” | OK | | non | negation particle | না | “not” | OK | | ciberà | future “will feed / will eat” | খাবেন | “will eat” | OK | | terra | “land, earth” | ভূমি | “land” | OK | | né | coordinating “nor” (in a negative coordination) | বা | “or” (used after negation) | OK | | peltro | “goods, merchandise” | পণ্য | “goods” | OK | | ma | contrastive conjunction “but” | কিন্তু | “but” | OK | | sapïenza | abstract noun “wisdom” | জ্ঞান | “wisdom” | OK | | amore | abstract noun “love” | প্রেম | “love” | OK | | e (line 104) | coordinating “and” (list) | এবং | “and” | OK | | virtute | abstract noun “valor / virtue” | বীরত্ব | “valor” | OK | | e (line 105) | coordinating “and” (linking clauses) | এবং | “and” | OK | | sua | possessive adjective “his” | তার | “his” | OK | | nazion | “birthplace, nation of origin” | জন্মস্থান | “birthplace” | OK | | sarà | future copula “shall be” | হবে | “will be” | OK | | tra | preposition “between” | মধ্যে | “between/among” | OK | | feltro (1st) | proper name “Feltro” (first endpoint) | ফেল্ত্রো | “Feltro” | OK | | e (second) | coordinating “and” (between the two place names) | এবং | “and” | OK | | feltro (2nd) | proper name “Feltro” (second endpoint) | ফেল্ত্রোর | “Feltro‑[genitive]” | **UNNECESSARY** (the genitive suffix “‑র” is added for Bengali syntax but is not present in the source) |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *ফেল্ত্রোর* – the added genitive marker “‑র” is required by Bengali grammar to express “between X and Y”, but it does not correspond to any morpheme in the source word *feltro*. No other tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically incorrect.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bengali script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bengali text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
